coverage.main: Read all fifteen pages of arXiv 1802.09707 (technical report): Sections 1-7, Tables 1-6, Figures 1-4, references and Appendices A-B (step-size Figure 5, one-step and Top-1 ensemble Tables 7-9). The corpus lists only the arXiv record.
coverage.supplement: Appendices are embedded in the arXiv PDF and read.
coverage.excluded_results: Diagonal (source = target) cells are white-box. Figure 2 plots gradient similarity. Section 5 theory has no rates.

result_groups.locator: Section 3.4 (p. 5); Tables 1, 4-6; Figures 1, 3; Appendix Figure 5, Tables 7-9
result_groups.population: For each ImageNet experiment, 5,000 randomly selected validation images 'that can be correctly recognized by all the examined models' (1,000 for Appendix A); PyTorch pre-trained sources, targets and ensembles
result_groups.outcome: Top-1 (or Top-5 for targeted ensembles) success rate, Eq. 7: 100 x (1/N) sum over the set of adversarial pairs of 1[prediction != true label]
result_groups.evidence: Images are explicitly restricted to those all examined models classify correctly. Eq. 7 averages over 'a set of adversarial pairs' without stating whether source failures are retained; under the field-3 wording rule this bare formula stays unclear (consistency sweep, 25 September 2026).

result_groups.population: MNIST fully connected networks and CIFAR-10 models (lenet, resnet20/44/56, densenet); evaluation set not stated
result_groups.evidence: The correctness filter is stated only for ImageNet; Eq. 7 does not state whether source failures are retained (unclear under the wording rule).

result_groups.population: DenseNet121-source adversarial examples evaluated on ResNet34 under rotation, Gaussian noise, blur and JPEG
result_groups.outcome: destruction rate R: among images correctly classified clean and misclassified adversarially (on the evaluated model), the fraction correctly classified after transformation
result_groups.evidence: R is explicitly restricted to clean-correct images that the evaluated model misclassifies adversarially; it is a destruction outcome rather than a transfer rate.

f1.evidence: CIFAR-10 test accuracies are printed and MNIST accuracies bounded (>98%). ImageNet accuracies are deferred to an external website and plotted in Figure 1 only.

f2.evidence: ImageNet and destruction scopes are explicitly clean-correct (yes); MNIST/CIFAR scopes are unresolved. Positive conditioning evidence.

f3.evidence: No scope states that source failures are retained or removed: Eq. 7 averages over an unspecified set of adversarial pairs, and the destruction rate conditions on the evaluated model. Downgraded from group-level no in the 25 September 2026 consistency sweep.

f4.evidence: ImageNet one-decimal rates over the stated 5,000 images would map to unique counts, but they were not extracted cell by cell; MNIST/CIFAR denominators are unstated.

f5.evidence: Sign-gradient L-infinity attacks with explicit epsilon (e.g., 15 or 20 on ImageNet, 10 on CIFAR-10, 40 on MNIST, pixel scale 0-255).

f6.evidence: No code is linked; models are public PyTorch checkpoints but the sampled images and attack code are not released.

artifact_checks.result: Downloaded and hashed; no code or data release is linked.

bounds_checks.reason: Rates are conditional on clean correctness.
Test accuracies are reported, but the attacked set is not identified.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Field-3 group codes were downgraded from no to unclear in the pre-freeze consistency sweep because Eq. 7 does not state that all generated examples are kept (contrast rank 47, which names the generated examples as the denominator).
